title: Linear Regression Assumptions & Diagnostics
interviewAnswer: For inference, linear regression relies on assumptions about functional form, independent errors, variance structure and error distribution; for prediction, diagnostics still reveal misspecification, outliers and extrapolation risk.
keyPoints: Check leverage/influence, not just residual size.
why: Linear Regression Assumptions & Diagnostics appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: For inference, linear regression relies on assumptions about functional form, independent errors, variance structure and error distribution; for prediction, diagnostics still reveal misspecification, outliers and extrapolation risk. Check leverage/influence, not just residual size. Heteroscedasticity affects uncertainty estimates. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Residual variance increasing with fitted revenue suggests transformation, weighted/robust methods or different uncertainty estimates.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Linear Regression Assumptions & Diagnostics make?
How would you validate or debug Linear Regression Assumptions & Diagnostics in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
